task_instance: Audit a small sample npm project (package.json listing lodash 4.17.21, axios 0.21.1, request 2.88.2) for supply-chain risk, following the skill's mandated workflow: run scripts/collect.py to gather version-matched advisories, publisher concentration, staleness and install-script data into findings.json, then scripts/render.py to produce report.md.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire workflow is built around two scripts it repeatedly requires and explicitly forbids working around: 'uv run {baseDir}/scripts/collect.py <project-dir> --json <out-dir>/findings.json' and 'uv run {baseDir}/scripts/render.py <out-dir>/findings.json --out <out-dir>/report.md'. The skill package at /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/trailofbits__skills__supply-chain-risk-auditor contains only SKILL.md and LICENSE -- no scripts/ directory and no collect.py or render.py anywhere in the repository (confirmed with a repo-wide find). The skill text is explicit that hand-collecting the underlying data (maintainer counts, download stats, CVE history) via gh, web search, or memory is a rejected rationalization ('gh can give me maintainer counts faster than the collector... Measured wrong'), so producing the deliverable by any means other than the missing collector would violate the skill's own stated method and produce exactly the kind of wrong figures it says the scripts exist to prevent. With the required tooling absent from the skill's own package, the specified deterministic collect-then-render pipeline cannot be executed, so the core deliverable (findings.json + report.md carrying scripted, reproducible per-dependency risk data) cannot be produced as the skill defines it.
evidence: Created /tmp/.../exec_ext/trailofbits__skills__supply-chain-risk-auditor/sample-project/package.json with 3 representative dependencies. Ran `find /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/trailofbits__skills__supply-chain-risk-auditor -type f` which returned only SKILL.md and LICENSE (no scripts/ directory). Searched the whole skill-achievability-compiler tree for collect.py/render.py filenames related to this skill and found none. Confirmed `uv` (/root/.local/bin/uv) and `gh` (/usr/local/bin/gh) are both present in the runtime, so the blocker is not a missing runtime capability -- it is that the skill package itself never shipped the scripts its workflow depends on. Per the skill's own step 3 instruction ('If collect.py exits non-zero, it is refusing to report -- relay its message verbatim instead of retrying or working around it'), the correct action on a missing/failing collector is to stop and report rather than improvise a substitute measurement method, which is what was done here.
